approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded, score-ranked population of accepted molecules. Each first parent is sampled through weighted score bands; crossover samples a different accepted partner through the same band rule, while ordinary mutation uses only the first source. Connected-fragment recombination, optional finishing mutations and local graph walks produce a surplus pool of new canonical identities. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select the announced batch. Accepted results immediately enter learning and greedy survival. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange remains disabled.
approach.novelty: Change only how the two crossover sources are paired. A minimum-similarity transport coupling keeps each molecule's original prospective probability in the first role and in the partner role, and never allows an originally forbidden pair, while moving joint probability toward less similar accepted partners. Some formerly possible pairs may disappear. Earlier siblings changed score weighting, source access, first-draw scheduling, survivor retention or product lifetime; the older affinity and core-balancing rules also changed marginal allocation. This test instead changes dependence between the two source roles. Lower similarity, productive complete offspring and improved final scores are separate predictions, and the first does not establish either of the others.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's score-band partner law reacts to the first source only by excluding its identity; it does not use pair structure. This leaves a directly measurable pairing-dependence opportunity while preserving the allocation controls that have conditional support. All actual Parent summary.json and run.log files are present and successful. Its complete mean is 0.5956696497334577 with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747 and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent logs finds 75,961 outer attempts, 34,334 crossover requests, 69,600 fresh pool members and 4,350 accepted offspring: 629 beat their best generating parent, 258 advance the incumbent, and 2,401 later breed. Mean accepted-offspring score is 0.38525565081713703, mean best-generating-parent score 0.47045588221649665 and mean positive incumbent increment 0.02251032201692723. These are descriptive limits, not evidence that a different coupling will help. The exact first-weight, partner-weight, nonincumbent-first-access and distinct-partner removals n-be83d2b1a4bd, n-ee95752352ec, n-9da98b015a09 and n-60350f969287 lose paired means 0.07249577949932767, 0.05180750887063701, 0.05581647713547766 and 0.03199243583539332, respectively. They motivate preserving both prospective role marginals and self-exclusion, without additive attribution. Earlier binary-Parent affinity and inverse-core allocation n-a20706504e8f and n-69c038cb49ac activated but lost means 0.01597200876080433 and 0.020256296737091634 on their own older Parent; n-f68f386d4d9d preserved prospective first marginals through systematic blocks yet lost 0.04216145214436932 against the current Parent. A read-only single-objective transport audit on the 435 recorded current-Parent states finds certified strict expected-similarity reduction in all 435 (mean 0.0570696041489986; minimum 0.006255160526603687; maximum column residual 2.0816681711721685e-15). This historical same-state feasibility probe has no alternate offspring, oracle labels or endpoint effect. It also finds that expected best-parent score can move despite fixed individual-role marginals; that threshold is not controlled by this intervention. Audit source and complete state-level results are retained in .slots/round-0025-slot-0/plan_audit.py and plan_parent_audit.json.
hypothesis: Replace only the conditional crossover-partner sampler with a certified deterministic minimum-count-Tanimoto transportation coupling of the original two-role joint law, preserving both original prospective role marginals and every original zero-pair restriction while retaining the exact first-parent sampler and distinct source identities.

finding_summary.headline: Less-similar pairs reached accepted offspring, but the matched mean fell by 0.0371
finding_summary.insights: Preserving each role’s score exposure at a fixed population did not preserve the joint best-parent threshold or the quality of later adaptive populations. Expected best-parent score moved upward in 282 states and downward in 153 despite the fixed marginals. The Child recorded more parent-beating offspring (745 versus 629) and more incumbent advances (277 versus 258), but accepted offspring had lower absolute mean scores (0.37150 versus 0.38526), their actual best-parent references were weaker (0.44047 versus 0.47046), and positive incumbent increments were smaller on average (0.01896 versus 0.02251). Thus the extra local wins and reuse do not establish more productive exploration. Changed pairs did reach real complete products and feedback, so lack of downstream exposure does not explain the failed score prediction. The chemistry still spans many ring frameworks and includes recognizable aryl cyclic amines, alongside reactive attachments, questionable bridges and unresolved stereochemistry; the evidence does not identify any of these as the cause of the score loss. Lower count-feature similarity controls source dependence, but this fixed objective did not reliably produce better complete molecular arrangements under the tested conditions. The contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation and the chemical or RNG-mediated cause of the loss remain open.
finding_summary.results: The coupling worked as intended in all 435 encountered population states. At each fixed state it preserved each source’s original probability in both parent roles and every forbidden pair, while expected pair similarity fell from 0.7591 to 0.7029. Actual partner identity changed in 30,333 of 34,407 crossovers. Those changed pairs produced 1,277 accepted complete molecules; 683 later served as breeding sources. There were no solver fallbacks or incomplete evaluations. Nevertheless, final Top-1 macro mean fell from 0.59567 to 0.55854: a paired change of -0.03713, failing the registered +0.002 criterion. Six of fifteen task/seed cells improved and nine declined. Seed changes were -0.07451, +0.00075 and -0.03761. The largest losses were decoration hopping in seed 0 and the sitagliptin objective in seed 2. Seed dispersion fell from 0.02659 to 0.00544, which does not establish reliable improvement.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, cyclic amines and fluorinated heterocycles coexist with reactive attachments and unresolved ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-5449c5ae9486 produces compact aromatic amides and ketones, nitrogen-rich linked heterocycles, aryl cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated diones or imino-amides. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against code Parent n-62daf219c70a: all supplied Child and published Parent trajectories for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 were present and read. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer proposals; there are no missing task trajectories, missing Parent paths, or absent matched seed comparisons. The supplied ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9609 to 0.9851 and aromatic-string incidences 0.931 to 0.9782. These measure the proportion of proposal strings containing a feature, not aromatic-atom fractions or scaffold diversity. Ring and aromatic chemistry are plainly available. Both formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task, although the molecules include protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because several leaders combine recognizable functional groups with N-halogen or O-F bonds, peroxides, short bridges across aromatic rings, unusual aromatic-labelled medium rings, or reactive halomethyl attachments. The conventional aryl piperidine leader is an important exception; these concerns are not universal. Overall drug-likeness is weak across the full output, with more recognizable medicinal chemistry in the cyclic-amine families. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, while leaders within individual seeds repeatedly revisit related arrangements; many different graph scaffolds do occur, so this is not global structural collapse. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not the retained best molecule of every seed. Per-task comparisons below use each complete trajectory and its recorded scores; displayed decimal scores are rounded. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions are offline RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES, documented with source hashes in .slots/round-0025-slot-0/molecular_audit.json and molecular_features.jsonl. Graph validity, aromatic perception and a high oracle label do not establish stability, synthesis or geometry. The inherited gaps originated in the Development-profile report for n-c55c3d520a2c and were carried into n-62daf219c70a; their current re-observation preserves that provenance. The present complete Parent pairing does not turn that earlier profile into an independent current-profile comparison. Chemistry associations here do not attribute liabilities, inherited fragments or endpoint changes to a particular algorithm component.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders have 25 heavy atoms, but their chemistry differs. Seed 0 produces an azaindole carboxamide with methoxy, methylthio and vinyl substituents and an N-fluoro anilide. Seed 1 instead leads with an N-methyl benzimidazole/pyridyl ketone carrying both a benzylic chloride and a chloromethyl ether. Seed 2 favors an N-N-bridged, partially unsaturated aryl framework bearing a tertiary N-methyl anilide, methoxy group and vinyl thioether; its graph has four perceived rings, including the pendant phenyl. These are compact, aromatic, carbonyl-containing molecules rather than simple chains. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2; ring-closure and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9724 and 0.9701. Familiar amide, ketone and heteroaryl chemistry coexists with environment-specific reactivity or bridge-geometry questions. Parent leaders instead include N-halogenated indole-like amide, diketone or cumulated-unsaturation families; the Child changes these arrangements without eliminating the chemistry concerns.
liabilities: N-F or N-Cl on an amide nitrogen and the chloromethyl/benzylic chloride attachments need local chemical-stability assessment; they should not be equated with ordinary aryl halogens.
The N-N bridge and unsaturation constrain the seed-2 topology; its representable graph and favorable label do not establish a feasible synthesis or conformation.
Late tiny proposals lose the aromatic and carbonyl context entirely, while late larger relatives can still score below the retained incumbent.
missing_features: The leading records do not establish conventional, less reactive replacements for the N-halogen amide, chloromethyl ether or benzylic chloride that preserve each family's score. The seed-2 non-N-halogen leader is a counterexample to an absolute need for that bond.

The bridged leader lacks an explicitly specified stereochemical identity and demonstrated accessible ring geometry. The record identifies no exact unseen target motif that can legitimately be prescribed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.305104808. The Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.420740853, 0.436818201 and 0.468683683, respectively; the corresponding published Parent leaders score 0.394051421, 0.474117018 and 0.438972502. Thus the seed-1 chemistry does not share the other seeds' direction. In a particularly close Child contrast, the seed-2 vinyl thioether at evaluation 258 scores 0.468683683, while replacing that linking sulfur with carbon to give the allyl analogue at evaluation 297 gives 0.338344080 with the rest of the recorded framework unchanged. This supports a local sulfur-environment association, not a universal sulfur requirement. The seed-0 N-F and N-Cl amide variants at evaluations 257 and 265 have the identical score 0.420740853, while the seed-2 leader contains no N-halogen bond. Isolated F at seed-0 evaluation 248 scores 0.0. The visible gradient favors contextual aromatic/carbonyl arrangements and particular substitutions; heteroatom or halogen presence alone is insufficient.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds diverge strongly. Seed 0 expands to a 55-heavy-atom leader containing several linked/fused nitrogen-rich aromatic dione units, N-O connectivity, an unsaturated linker and a brominated ether-bearing tail. Seed 1 instead has a 29-heavy-atom compact, densely cross-linked nitrogen/sulfur aromatic framework with an N-N link and a cyclic peroxide; short sulfur bridges create four-membered cycles across aromatic nitrogen-containing segments. Seed 2 leads with a 46-heavy-atom indane-like/heteroaryl dione assembly, aminopyridyl and imino linkages, a polyunsaturated tail and two O-F bonds. These are not interchangeable examples of one scaffold. Mean SMILES length is 81.2 and the maximum is 234, with ring-closure incidence 0.9793 and aromatic incidence 0.9782. Ring richness and extensive heteroatom functionality coexist with substantial synthetic and stability questions. The published Parent seed-0 leader is a much more compact linked fused heterocycle with carbonyl/thione, O-F and halomethyl-ether chemistry; Parent seeds 1 and 2 use different heteroaryl or peroxide-containing families.
liabilities: The O-F bonds, cyclic peroxide and brominated ether-bearing tail raise different local reactivity questions; a single generic halogen or oxygen count would obscure them.
Seed-1 short sulfur bridges across aromatic segments and dense cross-linking are geometrically questionable even though its heavy-atom count is modest.

Large repeated heterocyclic units and long unsaturated appendages add synthetic complexity without a consistent observed score advantage; tiny hydrocarbon outputs show the opposite loss of useful molecular context.
missing_features: The output does not establish robust, simpler, chemically credible alternatives preserving favorable linked heteroaryl/carbonyl relationships across seeds; a compact but strained peroxide/sulfur-bridge molecule is not evidence that compactness alone solves feasibility.

Conventional local alternatives to O-F, cyclic peroxide and short aromatic-spanning sulfur bridges are not demonstrated at each leader's score. The exact missing feature behind the stronger Parent seed-0 label is not identifiable from these unmatched scaffolds.
The polyunsaturated and imino tails lack explicit geometric-isomer identity. Their score benefit relative to specified isomers was not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.597950492, 0.617519320 and 0.620471918; the matched Parent values are 0.856147722, 0.624820660 and 0.617802403. In particular, the large seed-0 dione assembly does not recover the Parent's compact leading arrangement. The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381483, whereas acetylene at seed-0 evaluation 163 scores the observed floor of 0.5. Within the seed-2 linked heterocycle family, the distinct tail variants at evaluations 289 and 292 both score 0.619537418 despite different size and unsaturation. The favorable association is with retained complex aromatic/heterocyclic organization; neither adding more atoms nor preserving every distal tail detail has a demonstrated general benefit. The small positive seed-2 Parent difference and the other seeds' lower labels must remain separate; no single required missing decoration follows from these records.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders already contain available amines with substantial aromatic surface. Seed 0 gives a 25-heavy-atom bridged N-aryl cyclic-amine/polyamine framework with an aryl thiol and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 gives a recognizable 26-heavy-atom aryl piperidine with methoxy, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl-substituted phenyl groups. Seed 2 gives a 26-heavy-atom N-propyl azetidine joined through an ethyl segment to a brominated phenolic biaryl; one aryl ring also carries a fused four-membered O/CH2 ring. The azetidine is an ordinary saturated small-ring motif, whereas the fused oxygen ring poses a separate strain question. Mean SMILES length is 59.6 and halogen-string incidence 0.9839. Parent leaders include flexible tertiary aryl amines and pyrrolidine-containing fused-ring molecules, also with unassigned stereochemistry. The seed-1 piperidine is a more conventional synthetic framework than several of the other task leaders and is an important positive chemical counterexample.
liabilities: Seed-2 ring strain must be distinguished from the conventional azetidine; counting all small rings as equally problematic would be chemically misleading.
Some relatives add benzylic halides or N-Cl bonds, including the final seed-2 proposal, but the seed-1 and seed-2 leaders do not need such attachments.
Substantial aromatic/halogen content and unresolved configurations leave physical-property and stereochemical questions that the supplied labels do not answer.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identity is missing for the substituted cyclic amines and benzylic centres. A basic amine is not missing, and the absence of a formal charge symbol does not establish lack of protonatability.

A geometrically credible replacement for the seed-2 fused oxygen four-membered ring at its exact label is not established. The high-scoring seed-1 piperidine shows that this topology is not a universal requirement.

The near-ceiling labels do not identify a further absent receptor-binding feature; the demonstrable gaps concern molecular identity and feasibility rather than an inferred target-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.972085158, 0.996155819 and 0.999991691 against Parent values 0.999998918, 0.996975316 and 0.999993424. In contrast, the simple aryl methyl sulfone at seed-1 evaluation 13 scores 0.000321412 and an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/carbonyl fragment at seed-0 evaluation 17 scores 0.000438413. These are contextual comparisons, not controlled amine-removal experiments, but they associate the high labels with accessible aliphatic amines organized beside aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen or halogen count alone. The shorter 26-heavy-atom seed-2 leader scores 0.999991691; its 30-heavy-atom amino/fluorinated linker analogue at evaluation 250 scores 0.999989984. Extra linker atoms are therefore not necessary for a near-ceiling label. The conventional seed-1 piperidine also scores highly without an N-halogen bond or the fused oxygen four-membered ring. These oracle labels do not measure experimental binding, selectivity or chemical accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a 31-heavy-atom diaryl ether/tertiary-amine medium-ring framework bearing a saturated dicarbonyl nitrogen ring. Seed 1 reaches a 34-heavy-atom propyl/ethoxy-substituted polycyclic aryl framework containing adjacent ring nitrogens, a methylated amine, and ketone/lactam carbonyls. Seed 2 gives a 34-heavy-atom bridged diaryl ether with N-N connectivity and carbonyl-containing nitrogen-ring segments. The perceived cycle sizes include medium and large rings; the seed-1 graph includes an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen-containing cycle, whose notation does not establish a stable aromatic conformation. Mean SMILES length is 53.9, ring-closure incidence 0.9828, aromatic incidence 0.9759, and halogen incidence only 0.1. This chemistry supplies aromatic surfaces, nitrogen centres and carbonyl groups without relying on abundant halogens. Parent leaders also combine aryl/quinoline regions with nitrogen/carbonyl medium-ring or bridged systems, but with different connectivities.
liabilities: Dense bridges, medium-ring closures and constrained unsaturation make synthesis and conformation uncertain despite moderate heavy-atom counts.
N-N or N-O variants need assessment in their actual ring and carbonyl environments; the presence of an N-N bond alone is not a blanket instability verdict.
Ring richness and small local score gains coexist with unresolved geometry, so these quantities cannot serve as chemical-feasibility certificates.
missing_features: The leaders do not establish simpler, geometrically supported connectivities that retain the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization at the same labels.
The bridged and medium-ring products lack defined stereochemical/conformational identity; aromatic atom flags on a large cycle do not supply that information.
Several different frameworks occur across seeds, but within each leading family the record does not establish broad coverage of chemically independent, demonstrably feasible alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.167838659. Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.218217890, 0.237568874 and 0.231120084; the published Parent leaders score 0.225840399, 0.221409546 and 0.226003129. The seed-0 result therefore differs in direction from the other seeds. In seed 1, the leader at evaluation 256 scores 0.237568874 and the related structure with the ketone position reduced to a methylene at evaluation 264 still scores 0.232556132. In seed 2, insertion of a methylene into the N-N-containing ring segment changes 0.231120084 to 0.229673071. These nearby labels favor the broad aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement without making one ring size or carbonyl count uniquely sufficient. Methane at seed-1 evaluation 197 scores 0.0. The remaining score gap cannot be assigned to a missing named target motif from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a 26-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dione carrying N-F, a fluorinated cyclopentene, and an enol/imine-containing fluoroalkyl side chain. Seed 1 leads with a 30-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dione bearing two N-F bonds, a fluorocyclopropyl substituent and a fluorinated thiol-bearing lactam fused to an unsaturated larger ring. Seed 2 instead reaches a 23-heavy-atom single-benzene imino-amide with methoxy, methylamino and carbon-bound fluorine substituents, plus an N-amino alkynyl-amide segment extending into a fluoroalkene. It has neither the fused dione core nor an N-F bond. Mean proposal SMILES length is 47.5, aromatic incidence 0.931, ring-closure incidence 0.9609 and halogen incidence 0.8115. Compact fluorinated polar chemistry is present, but its local connectivity is frequently unconventional. The Parent's strongest seed-2 example had a small cyclic cumulene and a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; the current leaders use different chemistry, while N-F attachments recur in seeds 0 and 1.
liabilities: N-F on carbonyl-containing heterocycles, the N-amino alkynyl-amide segment and enol/imine tails require environment-specific stability and synthesis assessment; none is validated by the score.
Fluorinated saturated centres and alkene/imine arrangements are stereochemically unspecified. The thiol-bearing lactam and unsaturated ring geometry add separate local questions.
The current leaders avoid the Parent's leading cyclic cumulene, but this change alone does not establish better overall feasibility or explain the recorded score differences.
missing_features: The molecules do not establish consistently conventional fluorinated/polar arrangements with resolved tautomeric and geometric identity at the leaders' scores. The single-ring, non-N-F seed-2 leader is a real alternative family, not proof that fused rings or N-F are required.
Stereochemically specified saturated-ring products and stable local alternatives to the N-fluorinated diones are not demonstrated. Any score benefit from specifying them remains unmeasured.

The evidence does not identify an exact absent drug-like target scaffold or pharmacophore. Adding nitrogen, fluorine or rings indiscriminately would ignore the very low labels of the large initial/early molecules and tiny fragments.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.545501720, 0.520017184 and 0.495324126, versus Parent values 0.651021191, 0.487005731 and 0.720885367. Thus seed 1 rises while seeds 0 and 2 do not. The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.002094453, and the oversized 54-heavy-atom acetal/dione assembly at seed-1 evaluation 13 scores 2.192995343284275e-43. In seed 0, adding one methylene between the leading heterocycle and cyclopentene changes 0.545501720 to 0.492534554. A cleaner seed-2 local contrast retains the full imino-amide/alkynyl arrangement: the aryl-F compound at evaluation 282 scores 0.487225758, while its aryl-Cl replacement at evaluation 297 scores 0.108859974. This supports a context-specific fluorine/size association, not a universal fluorination prescription or need for N-F. The single-ring seed-2 leader and the close seed-1 benzenoid lactam relative scoring 0.518998130 also prevent treating the most elaborate ring system as required. The changed scaffold families do not isolate why the Parent's seed-2 label was higher.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally recorded under the Development profile in n-c55c3d520a2c and carried into n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-5449c5ae9486 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and batch size 10. Current leaders include N-F amides/diones, O-F bonds, a cyclic peroxide, and chloromethyl or benzylic-chloride attachments. Conversely, a conventional aryl piperidine and a single-ring imino-amide with carbon-bound fluorine are high-scoring within their own records without N-halogen bonds. The deficit is local chemical context, not an inability to make amines, heterocycles or ordinary carbon-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically appropriate substituent alternatives that preserve favorable functional-group relationships learned from accepted feedback. Distinguish heteroatom-halogen and activated benzylic environments from ordinary carbon-bound halogens, and assess N-N or peroxide bonds in their actual context. These associations do not establish a score benefit from a universal filter or identify the algorithm component responsible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This retains the gap originating in Development-profile n-c55c3d520a2c and carried by n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed for n-5449c5ae9486 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 observations per task and batch size 10. Current examples include four-membered sulfur bridges across aromatic nitrogen segments, a fused aryl O/CH2 four-membered ring, an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen cycle, and dense medium-ring bridges. Conventional saturated piperidine and azetidine motifs also occur; the current fluorinated leaders do not reproduce the Parent's leading small cyclic cumulene. The gap changes form rather than demonstrating a universal failure of small rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently connect ring-graph validity with credible bridge geometry, unsaturation and aromatic conformation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need to distinguish ordinary small saturated rings from problematic aromatic-spanning bridges or constrained unsaturation, and to offer geometrically credible alternatives preserving learned functional arrangements. Perceived aromaticity and ring counts cannot provide that assessment. No blanket prohibition on small, fused or medium rings, and no causal endpoint benefit, follows from this evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This was recorded in Development-profile n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in n-62daf219c70a. In current n-5449c5ae9486, all supplied Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and batch size 10 again have stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 on every task. The full optimizer trajectories also contain no slash-based alkene stereo notation. Substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged frameworks contain potential stereogenic environments. Formal-charge incidence is also 0.0, but clearly protonatable amines are present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after creating substituted saturated rings, bridges, alkenes and imines.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, while distinguishing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism are separate questions. These records establish unspecified identity, not a measured penalty, a required isomer, or attribution to the current pairing intervention.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap originates in Development-profile n-c55c3d520a2c and is carried by n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-5449c5ae9486 under Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10. Current trajectories include late isolated halogens and hydrocarbons at observed score floors, as well as large repeated heterocyclic assemblies. A 55-heavy-atom linked dione family does not recover its corresponding Parent's compact leading arrangement. Conversely, a 26-heavy-atom aryl cyclic amine and a 30-heavy-atom extended relative both receive near-ceiling labels, and different unsaturated tails can receive identical labels. Useful simplification is already possible; small size is not the deficit.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful molecular context while controlling redundant size and attachment elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Feedback-informed transformations should retain the molecular relationships that carry useful signal while testing simplification or replacement of dispensable portions. The missing capability is consistent control of context loss and elaboration. Neither a fixed minimum size nor a general preference for larger or smaller molecules follows, and the unmatched Parent/Child scaffold examples do not isolate a size effect.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This preserves the conditional coverage gap recorded in Development-profile n-c55c3d520a2c and carried by n-62daf219c70a. For n-5449c5ae9486 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, leading records repeatedly vary substituents, short linkers or ring segments within aromatic amide, linked heterocycle, aryl cyclic-amine and bridged carbonyl families. Different seeds produce substantially different families, and the full trajectories contain many typed and generic ring frameworks. Therefore the supported gap is useful, chemically credible alternative coverage near a leading arrangement, not absence of graph diversity or inability to create rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate reliable access to chemically independent feasible alternatives to an awkward leading family within each run.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold transformations need to reorganize learned favorable functional relationships into independently plausible connectivities, with accepted feedback determining where those alternatives matter. Distinct strings or framework counts alone do not establish useful chemical coverage. The historical provenance and current evaluation conditions must remain attached to this hypothesis; neither greater diversity nor altered source pairing is established here as its cause or solution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

method_references.title: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.
